newsitem.title: CROATIA: IMF to visit Croatia May 7-19 - agency.
newsitem.headline: IMF to visit Croatia May 7-19 - agency.

text.p: A delegation of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is visiting Croatia this week and next to evaluate the country's adherence to a three-year programme, Croatian Hina news agency said on Tuesday.

The IMF team, staying from May 7 to 19, is scheduled to meet representatives of the government, the central bank, the agency for the overhaul of banks, several ministries and other state institutions, Hina quoted a central bank statement as saying.
"The first results in the realisation of the three-year programme will be evaluated in the talks, as well as the possiblities for its further successful implementation," the statement said.
Croatia won a $486 million loan in support of its economic reforms from the IMF in March. The money is supposed to help the country press ahead with key structural reforms in the next three years.

To secure further IMF aid under a so-called extended fund facility (EFF), Croatia had to adopt a variety of medium-term policies in the monetary and fiscal sphere. They were approved by the Fund as a base for the new loan.

The country also has to make progress in developing fledgling financial markets and setting up a proper infrastructure, introducing a new payments system and also complete the privatisation of the economy. -- Davor Huic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4551-840
